newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Delhaize says 1996 turnover up 11.7 perc.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Delhaize says 1996 turnover up 11.7 perc.

text.p: Belgian retailer Etablissements Delhaize Freres et Cie "Le Lion" SA said on Friday 1996 consolidated turnover rose 11.7 percent to 411.6 billion Belgian francs ($12.7 billion) from 368.5 billion in 1995.
At the end of December 1996 the Delhaize group operated 1,700 sales outlets against 1,610 a year earlier.
The company added in a statement it expected consolidated profit to be 15 to 20 percent higher in 1996 than in the previous year.
It also expected to pay a higher dividend.
"The growth of the Delhaize "Le Lion" group will continue in 1997 thanks to the opening of more than 200 sales outlets," the company said.

In Belgium Delhaize sales, including value added tax (VAT), totalled 106.9 billion francs, up 3.3 percent, and 36 new outlets were opened. In 1997, 30 more would be opened and two billion francs of capital expenditures had been budgeted for.

In the United States, Food Lion sales rose 9.7 percent to $9 billion. Food Lion will consolidate recently acquired Kash 'n Karry from the 1997 financial year onwards. In Atlanta Super Discount Markets sales fell 6.1 percent to $275 milliion.
In France P.G. sales rose 6.3 percent to 2.1 billion French francs.
In Greece Alfa-Beta sales rose 16.8 percent to 95.3 billion drachma, and in the Czech Republic Delvita sales soared 54.7 percent to 3.7 billion Czech crowns.
